mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly expresses Newton’s third law of motion?

options.A: If a body A exerts a force on body B, then body B exerts a force of the same magnitude on body A, but in the opposite direction.
options.B: If a body A exerts a force on body B, body B will move in the same direction as the force applied by A.
options.C: The force exerted by a body depends on its mass and the acceleration it experiences.
options.D: An object at rest will remain at rest unless a net external force acts on it.

mcqs.answer: If a body A exerts a force on body B, then body B exerts a force of the same magnitude on body A, but in the opposite direction.
mcqs.explanation: Newton’s third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction: the forces are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on different bodies. Option A captures this precisely. Option B confuses the direction of motion with the direction of the reaction force. Option C describes Newton’s second law, and Option D describes Newton’s first law.

mcqs.question: A person pushes a wall with a force of 30 N. Which of the following correctly identifies the action–reaction pair?

options.A: Action: person’s push on the wall; Reaction: wall’s push on the person.
options.B: Action: wall’s push on the person; Reaction: person’s push on the wall.
options.C: Action: person’s push on the wall; Reaction: person’s own backward motion.
options.D: Action: wall’s push on the person; Reaction: wall’s deformation.

mcqs.answer: Action: person’s push on the wall; Reaction: wall’s push on the person.
mcqs.explanation: According to Newton’s third law, the force exerted by the person on the wall (action) is paired with an equal and opposite force exerted by the wall on the person (reaction). Option A states this correctly. Options B reverses the pair, while C and D introduce unrelated effects that are not the reaction force.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that the forces act on different bodies
mcqs.question: Which comparison best illustrates the fact that the action and reaction forces act on different bodies?

options.A: When a book rests on a table, the weight of the book and the normal force from the table act on the book.
options.B: When a rocket expels gas downwards, the upward thrust on the rocket and the downward force on the expelled gas act on the rocket.
options.C: When a magnet attracts a nail, the magnetic force on the nail and the magnetic force on the magnet act on the nail.
options.D: When a car accelerates, the engine’s force and the frictional force both act on the car.

mcqs.answer: When a rocket expels gas downwards, the upward thrust on the rocket and the downward force on the expelled gas act on the rocket.
mcqs.explanation: In the rocket example, the action force (rocket pushing gas down) and the reaction force (gas pushing rocket up) act on different bodies – the gas and the rocket. Option B captures this correctly. Option A describes two forces on the same body (the book). Option C incorrectly says both forces act on the nail. Option D describes two forces on the same body (the car).

mcqs.learning_point: Apply the law to everyday examples
mcqs.question: A swimmer pushes water backwards with her hands to move forward. Which statement correctly applies Newton’s third law to this situation?

options.A: The swimmer experiences a forward force equal in magnitude to the backward force she exerts on the water.
options.B: The water pushes the swimmer forward only if the swimmer’s hands are moving faster than the water.
options.C: The swimmer’s forward motion is due to the water’s resistance, not because of any reaction force.
options.D: The swimmer and the water exert forces on each other, but the forces are not equal because the swimmer is heavier.

mcqs.answer: The swimmer experiences a forward force equal in magnitude to the backward force she exerts on the water.
mcqs.explanation: Newton’s third law tells us that the force the swimmer applies on the water (action) is met with an equal and opposite force on the swimmer (reaction), propelling her forward. Option A states this correctly. Options B, C, and D either add unnecessary conditions or contradict the law by claiming unequal forces.

mcqs.question: Newton’s third law of motion can be stated as:

options.A: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
options.C: An object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.D: The acceleration of an object is inversely proportional to its mass.

mcqs.answer: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
mcqs.explanation: Option A directly states Newton’s third law. Options B and D refer to the second law, while Option C describes the first law.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of an action–reaction pair?

options.A: A book resting on a table and the gravitational force on the book.
options.B: A car’s engine pushes the car forward and the friction between tires and road.
options.C: A person pulling a rope and the rope pulling the person.
options.D: A magnet attracting a piece of iron and the magnetic field lines between them.

mcqs.answer: A person pulling a rope and the rope pulling the person.
mcqs.explanation: When a person pulls a rope, the rope exerts an equal and opposite pull on the person – a classic action–reaction pair. Option A involves two forces on the same body (gravity and normal). Option B describes forces that both act on the car. Option D describes a magnetic interaction but does not explicitly state the equal and opposite forces on different bodies.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that the forces act on different bodies
mcqs.question: Why do the action and reaction forces never cancel each other out?

options.A: Because they act on the same body but in opposite directions.
options.B: Because they act on different bodies, so each body experiences only one of the forces.
options.C: Because the reaction force is always smaller than the action force.
options.D: Because they occur at different times.

mcqs.answer: Because they act on different bodies, so each body experiences only one of the forces.
mcqs.explanation: Newton’s third law forces are equal and opposite but act on different objects; therefore they cannot cancel on a single object. Option B correctly explains this. Options A, C, and D are misconceptions.

mcqs.learning_point: Apply the law to everyday examples
mcqs.question: When you jump off a small boat onto a dock, the boat moves backward. Which statement best explains this using Newton’s third law?

options.A: Your feet push the dock forward, and the dock pushes you backward.
options.B: You exert a backward force on the boat, and the boat exerts an equal forward force on you.
options.C: The water provides an upward buoyant force that pushes the boat backward.
options.D: Your mass is transferred to the boat, causing it to move.

mcqs.answer: You exert a backward force on the boat, and the boat exerts an equal forward force on you.
mcqs.explanation: When you push against the boat to jump, you apply a backward force on the boat (action); the boat applies an equal forward force on you (reaction), propelling you forward and the boat backward. Option B captures this. Option A mixes up the objects, Option C introduces buoyancy unrelated to the action, and Option D is incorrect physics.
